title: Multisource Domain Metalearning Network for Battery State-of-Health Estimation Under Multitarget Working Conditions
authors: Mengqi Miao; Chaoang Xiao; Jianbo Yu
real_world_problem: Multiple target operating conditions cause domain shift; single-target adaptation must be retrained for each new condition.
method: Multisource domain meta-learning, meta-fusion, and an EMD recurrent-convolution feature extractor.
dataset: Combined lithium-ion battery dataset; exact constituent datasets not disclosed in the abstract metadata.
protocol_or_scope: Multiple source/target conditions with SOH labels for evaluation.
reported_metrics: MAE 0.0474 and normalized RMSE 0.2187 over three target operating conditions (units/normalization require full-text confirmation).
limitations_or_missing_data: Use as evidence for the pain point, not as permission to replace TimesNet/iTransformer.
gmtc_compatibility_observation: High conceptual fit for cross-temperature/load validation, but the full meta-learning network would be too large as a single add-on.
abstract: State of health (SOH) estimation is important in battery health prognostics. The discrepancy in working conditions gives rise to the phenomenon of domain shift, which presents a significant obstacle to the accurate estimation of battery SOH. Domain adaptation (DA) has been widely used to solve the domain shift problem in battery SOH estimation by minimizing the distribution discrepancy between different domains. However, the multitarget domain shift problem is not be addressed well for existing methods. Most existing DAs only consider a single target domain, which means that the model needs to be retrained when new scenarios emerge, which differ from the original target working condition. In this article, multisource domain metalearning network (MSDMLN) is proposed for battery SOH estimation under multiple target working conditions. A novel metalearning method, multisource domain metalearning (MSDML) strategy is developed for enhancing the generalization of the network by diversifying battery health degradation features based on meta fusion block. Empirical mode decomposition-densely connected recurrent-convolution network is developed to extract global degradation tendency and local fluctuation features of Li-ion batteries. The effectiveness of MSDMLN is verified on the combined Li-ion battery dataset. The results demonstrate that MSDMLN achieved low mean absolute error (i.e., 0.0474) and normalized root mean square error (i.e., 0.2187) for three different target operating conditions, which is better than other state-of-the-art methods. This illustrates the outperformance of MSDMLN in generalizing the estimation of battery SOH under multitarget working conditions, due to the integration of MSDML and the meta fusion block.

title: State of Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Battery With Label-Free Data Based on Deep Domain Feature Independent Alignment Network
authors: Chenxi Song; Haitao Yuan; G. Wang; Naxin Cui
real_world_problem: Target batteries lack SOH labels and differ by temperature, chemistry, and charge/discharge strategy.
method: Lightweight deep domain feature independent alignment with dynamic convolution and feature-space independent alignment.
dataset: Three lithium-ion datasets across temperatures, materials, and operating conditions; names absent from abstract metadata.
protocol_or_scope: Source labels plus early unlabeled target charging sequences.
reported_metrics: 30% early target charging data used without labels; average MAE 0.0098; relative improvements reported against GRU-FIAN, DANN, and LSTM.
limitations_or_missing_data: Would require a new protocol and domain-alignment loss; cannot be claimed using B0007/B0018 adaptation labels.
gmtc_compatibility_observation: Moderate-to-high conceptual fit, but current 60/20/20 protocol uses target labels and is not label-free.
abstract: Estimating the state of health (SOH) of batteries is critical for ensuring the battery’s safe operation and extending its service life. However, the accuracy and application of SOH estimation methods are limited by insufficient labeled training data and different usage scenarios. To address these issues, a label-free SOH estimation method for lithium-ion batteries is proposed, which is based on a lightweight deep domain feature independent alignment network (DDFIAN) model. In this model, dynamic convolutional layers with a convolutional kernel attention mechanism are designed as feature extractors to capture both domain-invariant and domain-specific features from battery charging data. On this basis, feature space independent alignment (FSIA) methods are utilized to enable unsupervised SOH estimation transfer learning, allowing the DDFIAN model to effectively learn the shared features of the source and target domain battery datasets while preserving the battery-specific information. Finally, the proposed method is validated on three lithium-ion battery datasets under varying temperatures, materials, and operating conditions (charge and discharge strategies). The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively estimates SOH in multicondition transfer learning scenarios, using 30% of the early stage unlabeled charging data from the target domain. The method achieves an average MAE of 0.0098, improving SOH estimation accuracy by 50%, 70%, and 90% compared to the GRU-FIAN, DANN, and LSTM models, respectively.

title: State of Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Using Data Augmentation and Feature Mapping
authors: W. Yao; Rucong Lai; Yong Tian; Xiaoyu Li; Jindong Tian
real_world_problem: Small battery datasets are slow to collect and models adapt poorly across batteries.
method: GAN augmentation with consistent Gaussian noise plus a feature-mapping module to reduce cross-dataset differences.
dataset: Multiple battery datasets/samples; exact names absent from abstract metadata.
protocol_or_scope: Limited source cycles and cross-battery evaluation data.
reported_metrics: About 87% of 60 samples improved after augmentation; average AE below 2%; feature mapping RMSE below 1% and half below 0.5%.
limitations_or_missing_data: Retain as baseline lineage evidence, not a second GAN innovation.
gmtc_compatibility_observation: Already overlaps the reproduced paper's SCF-GAN/small-sample premise; poor novelty as another main innovation.
abstract: Accurate state of health (SOH) estimation is crucial for the operating safety and reliability of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). Currently, data-driven SOH estimation methods have been widely used in both academic and industrial communities. Nevertheless, they are still confronted with challenges, including time-consuming data collection and poor adaptability to different batteries. This article proposes a deep learning framework with a generative adversarial network (GAN) for data augmentation and a feature mapping module. To make the GAN’s generator learn feature distribution of limited original data better, consistent Gaussian noise is applied to the same cycle sequence during data generation. In consideration of the prominent noises introduced by the GAN to short-cycle batteries, a feature mapping module is proposed to reduce the difference in features of different battery datasets. Experiments using estimators trained on different batteries and directly transferred to other batteries are carried out. Results indicated that the accuracy of about 87% of the total 60 samples is improved after data augmentation, and the average absolute error (AE) is below 2%. Furthermore, the embedded feature mapping module achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of lower than 1%, and half of them are below 0.5%.

title: Physics-Informed Deep Gated Recurrent Unit Network for Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Estimation Under Field Conditions
authors: Laijin Luo; Yu Wang; Yang Li; Qiushi Cui
real_world_problem: Field EV data have unreliable SOH labels, segmented charging, domain shift, and weak interpretability.
method: Capacity/uncertainty estimation with modified inverse ampere-hour integration and BEAST, feature screening, PIDGRU/DeepHPM, and Bayesian uncertainty-constrained training.
dataset: In-vehicle and cross-vehicle datasets; identifiers absent from abstract metadata.
protocol_or_scope: Segmented real-vehicle charging data and a defensible capacity/SOH reference process.
reported_metrics: MAE below 1.10% and RMSE below 1.31% across reported evaluations.
limitations_or_missing_data: Possible inspiration for uncertainty-aware partial-trajectory handling only after compatible public data are secured.
gmtc_compatibility_observation: Pain point is highly relevant, but copying the full PIDGRU/DeepHPM would violate the one-module and no-full-PINN constraints.
abstract: Accurate estimation of lithium-ion battery state of health (SOH) in electric vehicles (EVs) under real-world conditions is much more challenging than using well-designed laboratory cycling data due to unreliable SOH labeling and segmented charging behavior, and the results often lack interpretability. To address these issues, this article proposes a physics-informed deep gated recurrent unit (PIDGRU) architecture for robust and interpretable SOH estimation without requiring explicit physical modeling. First, a modified inverse ampere-hour integral method is combined with the Bayesian estimator of abrupt, seasonality, and trend (BEAST) algorithm to estimate battery capacity and characterize SOH uncertainty. A universal feature extraction and selection framework is then developed to handle segmented EV charging data, utilizing a hybrid linear–nonlinear redundancy analysis to ensure an optimal input feature set. The PIDGRU integrates empirical degradation modeling and nonlinear dynamic degradation learning through a deep gated recurrent unit (GRU) network, utilizing a deep hidden physics model (DeepHPM). A Bayesian inference uncertainty-constrained (BIUC) strategy is introduced to enhance training reliability and uncertainty quantification. Extensive evaluations on both in-vehicle and cross-vehicle datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy, robustness, and generalizability, with the mean absolute error (MAE) and root-mean-squared error consistently below 1.10% and 1.31%, respectively.

title: Transfer Learning-Based Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Estimation With Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy
authors: Mingqiang Lin; Dingcai Hu; Jinhao Meng; Ji Wu
real_world_problem: SOH models must generalize across temperature and cell type while retaining physical interpretability.
method: Equivalent-circuit features from EIS, spatiotemporal LSTM, and transfer learning.
dataset: Two public EIS datasets; names absent from abstract metadata.
reported_metrics: Overall RMSE below 1.9%; more than 80% accuracy improvement over ST-LSTM reported by authors.
limitations_or_missing_data: Do not add EIS merely to chase accuracy; it changes sensing assumptions and available inputs.
gmtc_compatibility_observation: Low direct feasibility because the current HF/STL pipeline does not use dense EIS spectra.
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are utilized as energy storage units in mobile devices, electric vehicles, and other fields. To ensure the safety and reliability of batteries, the prediction of the batteries’ state of health (SOH) is one of the key technologies. This article proposes a transfer learning-based lithium-ion battery SOH estimation method using explainable electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). EIS has advantages such as explainability, rapid response, and noninvasiveness. Benefiting these, the physical parameters are extracted as the battery aging features by fitting an equivalent circuit model with the EIS measurement. To increase the representational power of the model and capture the complex sequential styles, a spatiotemporal long short-term memory (LSTM) network model is built to extract the time series features. Finally, the battery degradation features are fit through a fully connected layer. To improve the model’s generalization, a transfer learning strategy is added to estimate the SOH of the target cell by fine-tuning the initial model parameters on different temperatures and different types of cells. The proposed method, TL-ST-LSTM, has been validated on two public datasets, with an overall root-mean-square error (RMSE) error controlled within 1.9%. Compared to the spatiotemporal LSTM (ST-LSTM) method without transfer learning, the accuracy has been improved by over 80%. In addition, it also demonstrates an improvement in accuracy compared to existing transfer learning methods, such as TL-CNN and TL-LSTM.

title: Aging and Performance Analysis of 18650 Lithium-Ion Cell Capacity Degradation: Data-Driven Insights and Modeling
authors: Víctor Olivero-Ortiz; Ingrid Oliveros; Carlos A. Robles-Algarín
real_world_problem: Second-life screening needs interpretable, low-cost operational indicators and predictive uncertainty.
method: Cycle segmentation, cycle-time/internal-impedance indicators, and Gaussian-process regression with multiple kernels.
dataset: Two 18650 cells, 99 cycles, under 3C/1C and 2C/2C profiles from an open degradation dataset.
protocol_or_scope: Voltage, current, temperature, cycle time, capacity, and optionally DC impedance.
reported_metrics: Best charge RMSE 2.217-4.606 mAh; discharge RMSE 3.166-3.518 mAh; cycle time outperformed impedance-only features.
limitations_or_missing_data: Useful counter-evidence that feature relevance can matter more than a complex neural architecture.
gmtc_compatibility_observation: Moderate fit for uncertainty or operational-feature diagnostics; small two-cell evidence limits generalization.
abstract: This work analyzes and models degradation in 18650 lithium-ion cells using segmented experimental charge–discharge data (99 cycles under two cycling profiles, 3C/1C and 2C/2C). Beyond raw electrical and thermal measurements (voltage, current, and temperature), we derive operational indicators—mainly cycle time (charge/discharge duration) and internal impedance—to capture nonlinear relationships with capacity. Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) with multiple kernels (RBF, Rational Quadratic, Matérn, plus white noise) is used to predict capacity from these features. Quantitative results indicate that cycle-time features are the most predictive variables. During charging, the top configurations achieve RMSE values of 2.217–4.606 mAh and MAE values of 1.411–3.290 mAh across two cells. During discharge, the best models reach RMSE values of 3.166–3.518 mAh and MAE of 2.186–2.192 mAh. In contrast, impedance-only settings produce significantly higher errors — RMSE approximately 138–182 mAh during charging and roughly 11.281–11.683 mAh during discharging (MAE approximately 9.159–9.416 mAh) — demonstrating their limited usefulness when used alone under the studied regimes. These results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed GPR plus operational features methodology and show that feature selection has a greater impact on accuracy than kernel choice. The approach delivers low absolute error, stable predictive distributions, and consistent phase performance, supporting SOH/RUL estimation and second-life cell screening. The cycle segmentation based on fragmentation further improves interpretability and model design, offering a practical route toward reliable battery management and sustainable second-life applications.

title: Battery State of Health Estimation via Federated Learning on Diverse Data from Multiple Sources
authors: V. Dimitrievska; Andrea Urgolo; Manuel Freiberger; K. Unger
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Federated Learning and Intelligent Computing Systems (FLICS)
real_world_problem: Models are confined to individual chemistries and laboratory datasets; distributed data cannot always be shared.
method: Comparison of federated-learning strategies over heterogeneous multi-source SOH datasets.
dataset: Three public datasets; names and quantitative results absent from abstract metadata.
protocol_or_scope: Multiple partitionable datasets representing separate clients/sources.
reported_metrics: Abstract reports a detailed performance assessment but provides no numeric metric.
limitations_or_missing_data: Evidence for heterogeneity/privacy as a gap; not yet a suitable minimal module.
gmtc_compatibility_observation: Low-to-moderate: realistic but introduces a distributed training system, which is too broad for one clean G-MTC innovation.
abstract: Accurate battery health estimation is crucial for ensuring the safety, reliability, and optimal performance of electric vehicles. In recent years, machine learning models have achieved high accuracy in predicting battery State-of-health (SOH), but their performance typically remains limited to specific battery chemistries and custom laboratory datasets. To address this limitation, our work aims to develop and evaluate a unified SOH prediction framework capable of learning from diverse battery types and heterogeneous datasets collected across multiple sources. This approach represents a step toward future largescale, privacy-preserving SOH modeling, where models can be continuously improved using distributed private datasets without requiring direct data sharing. In this paper, we evaluate several federated learning strategies for battery SOH prediction applied to three public datasets, and we provide a detailed performance assessment alongside an analysis of the key challenges associated with learning from heterogeneous and distributed battery data.

title: Battery Time-Series Data Augmentation Using a GAF-Based Generative Framework
authors: Opy Das; Xin Sui; Filippo Sanfilippo; S. Rudra
real_world_problem: Battery time-series data are scarce for downstream state estimation.
method: Gramian angular field encoding, DCGAN image synthesis, and inverse GAF reconstruction.
dataset: MIT battery dataset; voltage, current, and temperature sequences.
protocol_or_scope: Dense time-series signals suitable for GAF conversion.
reported_metrics: Augmented data improved downstream SOC estimation; abstract metadata gives no exact SOH/RMSE result.
limitations_or_missing_data: Exclude as the main innovation despite thematic relevance.
gmtc_compatibility_observation: Low novelty because G-MTC already contains SCF-GAN; replacing it would violate the frozen architecture.
abstract: Generative models have gained significant attention in computer vision and natural language processing for their ability to generate realistic samples from complex data distributions. Inspired by these advancements and the persistent challenge of data scarcity in time-series domains, this work proposes a pioneering framework that transforms time-series data (e.g., voltage, current, temperature of lithium-ion batteries) into Gramian Angular Field (GAF) images for synthetic data generation using deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DCGAN) architecture. The proposed GAF-based GAN framework, validated on the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) battery dataset, generates samples that closely resemble real data and enables accurate signal reconstruction through inverse GAF transformation, effectively overcoming scale invariance and invertibility issues. To further demonstrate the quality of the synthetic signals, state of charge estimation (SOC) is performed using both original and augmented datasets. The results present that using augmented datasets help the models perform better than when trained only on the original data, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed method for improving time-series data augmentation and state estimation.

title: Explainable MFDWA-GRU Model for Battery State of Health Estimation
authors: Anantha Padmanabhan; S. Mate; Rajeev Kumar Singh; S. Singh
venue: IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Industrial Electronics
real_world_problem: SOH models need robustness across initial conditions, battery combinations, horizons, and interpretable feature influence.
method: Multibranch dilated TCN with attention/dynamic weights, GRU, and SHAP explanations.
dataset: Multiple datasets; names and numeric errors absent from abstract metadata.
protocol_or_scope: Multivariate degradation sequences and post-hoc SHAP computation.
reported_metrics: Authors report lower MAE/RMSE across multiple datasets, without numeric values in the retrieved abstract.
limitations_or_missing_data: SHAP could be a reporting tool, but is not by itself a predictive innovation.
gmtc_compatibility_observation: Moderate for diagnostics, low for replacing the existing TimesNet/iTransformer branches.
abstract: The operational safety of lithium-ion batteries is heavily dependent on accurate battery state of health (SOH) assessments. This article introduces a novel hybrid algorithm: A multifaceted temporal convolutional network with dynamic weight adaptation (MFDWA) combined with a gated recurrent unit (GRU) to estimate the SOH of lithium-ion batteries across various experimental setups. The MFDWA architecture includes multiple temporal convolutional network (TCN) branches, each containing a dilated TCN block, attention blocks, and dynamic weight adaptation components. This multibranch structure captures multiscale patterns through different dilation rates, while attention blocks select essential input features. The dynamic weight adaptation mechanism further enhances performance by addressing evolving battery dynamics. The GRU component tracks temporal information sequences by retaining relevant past states. The proposed hybrid algorithm performs better than the existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving lower mean absolute error and root mean square error values across multiple datasets while maintaining parameter compatibility. These results indicate the model’s robustness across different initial conditions, battery combinations, and varying prediction horizons. In addition, the integration of explainable artificial intelligence through the SHapley Additive exPlanations technique in the proposed hybrid model prioritizes input features, improves model performance, and enhances interpretability, thus fostering user trust.

title: An Innovative Magnetic Field Sensor based Method Predicting Lithium-ion Battery State-of-health
authors: Ze Hui; Mohamed Mamlouk; Jie Zhang; Deepayan Bhowmik
real_world_problem: Indirect BMS signals may miss structural aging and safety-relevant current inhomogeneity.
method: External magnetic-field sensing with PLSR and CNN models.
dataset: Dedicated magnetic sensor measurements during charge/discharge; sample details absent from abstract metadata.
protocol_or_scope: A magnetic sensing device not present in NASA data.
limitations_or_missing_data: Exclude unless new hardware data are legally obtained; do not synthesize missing sensor values.
gmtc_compatibility_observation: Very low implementation feasibility with current data despite strong application motivation.
abstract: As a portable energy storage device, lithium-ion batteries are widely used in various industries. However, with the increasing number of consumers, the number of accidents caused by the instability of aging lithium-ion batteries, such as spontaneous combustion due to thermal runaway, has also increased, raising significant safety concerns among consumers and manufacturers. Battery aging is fundamentally the result of structural changes within the cell, which are presented as phenomena such as swelling of the battery. These internal structural alterations lead to an inhomogeneous current distribution during operation, further exacerbating the instability of the battery. To address the above issue, we propose an innovative magnetic sensor-based battery state-of-health prediction method that differs from traditional state-of-health prediction approaches, such as data-driven models and equivalent circuit-based methods. Instead of relying on indirect data analysis, our approach employs a magnetic field sensing device to capture real-time variations in the battery magnetic field during charging and discharging. A traditional partial least squares regression(PLSR) model and a convolutional neural network (CNN) are trained to capture the evolving characteristics of the battery’s surface magnetic field, which grows increasingly inhomogeneous with aging. By directly utilizing the intrinsic properties of the battery instead of relying on secondary data analysis to infer lifespan, our method achieves a high R2 value of 0.92, providing a non-destructive, more precise, and reliable approach to predicting battery state-of-health.
